method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file: title and title.canDo, the Folge (9 lines, gist item, gloss), the three inputs (LS1 dialogue and menu, LS2 dialogue, LS3 dialogue and e-mail), the 6 H1 texts, the strategy card, both speaking parts (instructionsDe, situationDe, cards, openingLine, hintWords, 16 model turns, aiRole), the S1 situation, taskDe, 5 fields, checklist and model text, the 2 check lines, the 8 redemittel, both aussprache blocks, story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine, promptDe, option and explanation.de, the fact record, the rule cards rc.moegen and rc.akkusativ, and the 36 lexicon entries allocated to a1.1-u09 with their example sentences. We solved all 93 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line (1 Folge gist, 15 input, 12 structured-input, 33 pool, 16 reserve, 6 H1, 8 check, 2 proof), plus the 4 perception items and the 5 S1 fields, and checked the 15 generator slots against the lexicon roles (every lex.glossTyped source is productive, every lex.articlePlural source has a plural). For sentence_building we permuted the tiles, V1 questions included; for error_correction we tried every correction the named category admits. We ran 90 candidate learner answers through the real grader src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js (the S1 fields exactly as WritingTaskView FormTask builds them), e.g. „Mögt auch ihr Kuchen?“ (ls1-p09), „Ich nehme den Obstsalat.“ (ls2-p10), „Ich trinke einen Tee.“ (ls3-p10), „am Mittwoch“ (ls3-i05), „drei achtzig“ and „3,80 €“ (ls1-i03), „Kovalenko“, „OLENA KOVALENKO“ (f1), „am Freitagabend“ (f3), 28 time spellings (f4) and „Tisch für 6“ (f5). We compiled the level in memory (scripts/course-v2/lib/compiler.mjs compileLevel) and ran the live speaking functions on the compiled a11-u09-s entry (speakingAI.mjs normalizeSpeakingTask and buildCoursePartnerPrompt; speakingV2.mjs profile selection). We checked the exam blocks against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (h1: 6 × abc, 3 options, 2 plays, 32–53 words, text variant; sp2 cards-ask, 2 topics; sp3 cards-request, 2 cards; s1: 5 fields, 36–48-word situation) and recounted every text with the validator's wordCount (t1–t6 42/39/48/38/46/35, S1 44, e-mail 57, cliffhanger 24). We recomputed every sum against the LS1 menu (LS2 20,90; t2 6,40 → 8,90; t6 11,10; check 9,20; S1 head count Olena + 5 = 6). We ran the validator's own knownForms + licensedForms at a1.1-u09 over every German string of the file, including the surfaces LEX-01 does not walk (strategy card, openingLine, hintWords, model turns, aussprache focus, modelText, cliffhanger), and looked up each unknown token's allocation in all eight lexicons. We read cast and story against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (ensemble -1/-2 f, -3/-4 m), u08 (cliffhanger: Elif offers Priya a coffee after an hour of running), u10 (Sophie's call, „Bis Freitag im Restaurant!“, Dresden the day after the birthday) and u11 („Wir haben im Restaurant Kochi gegessen“). We re-read the two sources of fact a1.1-u09-f01 at gesetze-im-internet.de in this session (§ 13 Abs. 5 PAngV, § 107 Abs. 3 Satz 2 GewO). We verified every r1 finding against the current file, the lexicon, the rule cards, u10 and the rails, and compared the trail classes of a1.1-u04 r1–r5, u01 r2 and u08 r2.

verdict: Not exit-ready: 1 BLOCKER (owned by the speaking engine, not the unit), 2 MAJOR and 6 MINOR. The round-1 work is real: 12 of 15 findings are fixed or fixed in the unit, all three r1 blockers are gone and the validator is green. Every correction prompt names what to correct, the S1 key accepts the 12-hour time and „Personen“, the café scene now eats before it pays, the check scene belongs to other guests, t5 books another restaurant, Sp3 is neutral with „Kann ich bitte … haben?“, the deviation is logged and the Trinkgeld fact is sourced and current. We solved all 93 authored items and the 5 form fields blind, and every key is right. Three things stop exit. (1) F01, BLOCKER: the speaking engine still ignores `parts`. On the compiled a11-u09-s the AI partner runs a card round with no cards („Deine Karten: —“), never reaches Teil 3, and the grader scores only sd1-sp2. Teil 3 is this unit's Prüfungsfokus for Sprechen and carries two can-do proofs, so it is claimed but neither run nor scored. (2) F02, MAJOR: ls1-p09 rejects the standard focus order „Mögt auch ihr Kuchen?“ while accepting the colloquial „Mögt ihr Kuchen auch?“ — the order class of u04 and u08, let through because the order rail excludes questions. (3) F03, MAJOR: r1-F04 was closed with a 27-form list, and the S1 form still rejects „am Freitagabend“ (the unit's own phrase for this dinner) and „abends um halb acht“. The minors: an H1 distractor that is never heard (F04, the u04 r1-F19 class), lexicon debts left by r1 fixes (F05: a2.1's lx.getrennt duplicate is a LEX-07 blocker there; höflich without input; the receptive „Stück“ produced; the unit at the LEX-05 ceiling), and four owner-held carry-overs (detectors, recycling, rc.moegen, word cards). Unit edits are small: 1 accepted form (F02), 8 stop-gap accepted forms (F03, until the checker rule lands) and one t6 line with its explanation (F04).

findings.problem: The prompt asks only for the yes/no question, and the tiles build three grammatical ones. The item accepts the colloquial „Mögt ihr Kuchen auch?“ but rejects „Mögt auch ihr Kuchen?“, in which auch focuses the subject („do you too like cake?“). That is standard German, and it is the pattern u08 r2-F02 listed as „Kann auch Olena kommen?“. Accepting the rarer colloquial order while rejecting a standard one is exactly the shape of u04 r1-F04 („Dort ist die Butter auch.“ accepted, „Auch die Milch ist billig.“ rejected) and u04 r2-F02. ITM-09 passes because its order module declares questions out of scope. That is the gate hole u08 r2-F02 named, and the class is now in its third a1.1 unit (u04, u08, u09), with stop-the-line in force since u08 r2. A defensible second answer not accepted: MAJOR (§9.4).
findings.fix: Unit: add „Mögt auch ihr Kuchen?“ to accepted, with acceptedWhy „grammatisch: ‚auch‘ vor ‚ihr‘ betont ‚ihr‘ (auch ihr, wie wir)“. Or, if the item should drill V1 only, drop the „auch“ tile ([„ihr“, „mögt“, „Kuchen“] → „Mögt ihr Kuchen?“). Rule: see proposedRule.
findings.proposedRule: Extend lib-validate/orders.mjs to V1 yes/no questions (tiles without a W-word): after the finite verb, a focus particle (auch, nur, noch) may stand before the subject, pronoun or noun phrase, or after the object, and every such order the tiles build must be accepted unless promptDe fixes it. Fixtures: a1.1-u09 ls1-p09 („Mögt auch ihr Kuchen?“) and the a1.1-u08 item behind u08 r2-F02 („Kann auch Olena kommen?“). The test runs over all registered courses.
